title: Investigate Slow Integration Tests In Repo CLI Go
description:
Investigate why ~70 integration-style tests in repo/client/cli/go/main_test.go run against the real monorepo root (via findTestRepoRoot / GetRootDir()) instead of a t.TempDir() fixture, and are dramatically slower than expected:

1. TestBuildMonorepoTree (calls BuildMonorepoTreeCached in main.go ~line 7342) did not finish within 280s in isolation. Investigate why the disk cache (tree.lock / loadTreeCache ~line 7342-7375) doesn't make repeat calls fast against an unchanged repo, and whether the tree walk (isGitIgnored/StreamFiles, using sabhiram/go-gitignore) is pathologically slow (backtracking regex per path) at 230K files.

2. TestFoldersNonEmpty and TestFilesNonEmpty (GraphQL folders/files queries via getTestExecutor(t) ~line 850) take ~37-38s EACH even though sibling resolvers (bundles/contributors/tickets/policies/statutes) on the same executor return in under 1-2s. Investigate whether folders/files resolvers are missing a cache/index reuse that the other resolvers have (possibly related to the bleve full-text index under github.com/blevesearch/bleve_index_api).

3. TestCodebaseCommand (~line 2014) and TestNormalizeTicketFileInput (~line 1168) show cost/behavior that depends on test execution order because they read a shared package-level rootDir/GetRootDir() without resetting it — a test-isolation smell. Investigate whether this state should be isolated per-test (e.g. t.Cleanup restoring the previous root).

This is a pure investigation/root-cause task, not an implementation task — do not fix anything, just report findings with file:line references. Findings were surfaced during an unrelated test-level-assignment sweep where these tests were only reassigned to a slower "TestExhaustive*" tier as a workaround, not fixed.
summary: Root-caused all three questions with empirical verification, no code changed (pure investigation as requested). (1) The tree-cache disk cache in BuildMonorepoTreeCached is sound and not the bottleneck; cache misses are slow because isGitIgnored's go-gitignore library never matches bare directory paths against trailing-slash patterns (target/, __pycache__/, build/, etc.), so filepath.SkipDir never fires for those directories — not catastrophic regex backtracking (Go's RE2 has none), but a systematic directory-pruning miss. The repo's top-level /target alone has 1,676,267 files vs 14,767 git-tracked files. (2) folders/files GraphQL resolvers are ~40x slower than bundles/tickets/policies because they route through a third, completely separate, uncached walk (CodebaseContext.LoadFiles -> ScopeToFiles -> globByExtension) that shares no cache with BuildMonorepoTreeCached, and whose matchesIgnorePattern/LoadGitignore only reads the root .gitignore and never applies gitignore's implicit **/ anchoring, so nested target/, build/, __pycache__/ etc. anywhere below the repo root are never pruned at all (only top-level ones are) — verified empirically with a small Go program using the pinned doublestar version. (3) getTestExecutor (main_test.go:850) mutates the package-level rootDir without any defer/t.Cleanup restore and bypasses SetRootDir's cache invalidation; TestExhaustiveNormalizeTicketFileInput and TestExhaustiveCodebaseCommand read GetRootDir()/global state with zero root setup of their own, so their cost and correctness depend on whichever prior test in the same binary last touched rootDir. Full findings with main.go/main_test.go line references and empirical repro programs are in findings.md and scratch/gitignore-check/ in this ticket folder.
